correctness.rationale: For every nonempty antitone decreasing f on [n], min(domain)=d and max(image)=f(d)<=d; image∩domain either empty or {d}. Strict case gives f²=0; touching case gives f² constant d on the nonempty fiber f^-1(d), a rank-one idempotent, hence f³=f². For fixed domain/image of cardinalities w,h, the h positive consecutive inverse-image blocks number C(w-1,h-1). Strict union has w+h distinct points, giving C(n,w+h); touching has w+h-1 distinct points, giving C(n,w+h-1). Binomial series gives nonzero square total F_{2n}; shifting the strict domain down one unit bijects zero-square maps on [n] with all nonempty antitone decreasing maps on [n-1], giving F_{2n-1}-1. Standalone exhaustive checker confirms n=1..9 without being used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural semigroup-theoretic problem asks which antitone decreasing elements of a recently studied transformation monoid square to zero and which stabilize to nonzero idempotents. The theorem provides an all-n structural dichotomy, sharp width-height support thresholds, complete counts by both standard semigroup parameters, and a nontrivial split into distinct Fibonacci sequences, including all noninjective elements. These data describe second powers and nilpotence, not an arbitrary slice or mere recomputation of the already published total.
